Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Summary 2 Gameplay 2.1 Designate Suit 3 2-Player Rule 4 Custom Options Summary Try to collect as many positive points and as few negative points as possible with your tricks. However, you don't know which suit will generate positive or negative points in each round. The game lasts for 5 rounds. Each round there will be a designated number. According to the corresponding number card played, their suits gain trump, plus, hund, minus, lead effect according to their order. [ fast tutorial ] Gameplay Starting with the start player, each player plays exactly 1 card from their hand. You must follow the suit colour played first in that trick, if possible. After all players have played their cards, if the trump suit has been set and any trumps have been played, the player with the highest value trump wins the trick. Otherwise, the player with the highest value of the first played suit is the winner of the trick. The player takes all the cards in the trick. Designate Suit Whenever a card matches the value of the currently designated card number, an effect is immediately assigned to the suit of the effect. These effects are assigned according to the order they are played. Effects in order: 1. Trump : The suit is trump from now on. 2. Plus : These cards give positive points. 3. Hund : Each player takes 3 points except for players who have the most and least cards of this suit. 4. Minus : These cards give negative points. 5. Lead : The player with most lead suit cards decides who will be the lead player in the next round (After all players look at their cards in the next round). 2-Player Rule The game is setup like in a 3-Player game but with a virtual player. Half of the virtual player's hand is face up on top of the face down cards, from left to right. Virtual player moves like a third player. Rules: - Always play the left-most displayed legal card. - If there are any cards of the first played card suit in the virtual player's display, play the left-most of that suit. - After a trick ends, if there is a face down card without face up card on top, reveal it. Custom Options Use more cards : Use 9/9/12/15 cards of each suit instead of 6/6/8/10 in the 2/3/4/5-player mode. Select designation cards : Use all designation cards corresponding to the card values used in the game instead of 1-5. Starting from the second turn player, all players select a suit and a designation card in turn order until 5 sets are chosen. When a card matching a designated set is played, the suit of that card will be assigned to the next available suit power. [Rating: 4/10] Trick taking card game with a few twists by establishing trumps, points, negatives as the hand progresses. The issue I have is it feels a little too chaotic for me. There's not enough opportunity to make strategic decisions.

[Rating: 4/10] Interesting game that doesn't seem to work that well. For some portion of the game you're hardly playing because you don't know what anything is worth and then you are a lot of times forced to play. There are much better trick-taking games nowadays. I would give it another try.

[Rating: 4.4/10] trick taking game which can define different suits for different functions/scoring  2/10 5p game  quite random for 5p games and become dry after 2nd play  felt quite chaotic and random and have much other better choices for trick-taking games

[Rating: 5/10] Feb 2017: Gifted to a friend. Downgrade from 8 to 5. Too tactical and chaotic.  March 2016: Avoid the basic game! Go straight to the advanced variants that (a) add more cards to the deck and (b) allow players to choose the "fuck you" cards. The latter variant adds a huge layer of strategy and control to the game!  Tried the version with the two variants with three players only. BTW, I think it would take *forever* to get the winning condition of 19 points.

[Rating: 5/10] Found this game when looking at games during a math trade. Popped up and looked interesting. Trick taking with an interesting mechanic for determining the various roles of each suit in a given round. Definitely a cool twist on the genre, not sure the actual game play was there. Felt I didn't have much control when I was playing cards. One less suit would have been more ideal. Probably not designed for 3 players so playing with more players would probably help as well.
